candidates.attacker_control: The `theme` query-string parameter of the API tool page (documented runtime feature: `modules/jooby-apitool/README.md` lines 260-265, e.g. `/swagger?theme=material`). A value such as `x"><script>...</script>` is accepted verbatim, lowercased only by `toLowerCase()` (which does not remove markup), and reflected into the served page.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked for any escaping/validation of `theme`: `Options.theme()` (617-620) only null-checks; the handlers use the raw value; `Results.ok(...).type(MediaType.html)` and `BuiltinRenderer.text` do not encode; no CSP or `X-Content-Type-Options` header was found in the source. The docs enumerate expected theme names but the code never enforces them. By contrast, path-based 404 messages are explicitly escaped (`Request.path(true)`), which shows escaping was considered elsewhere but not here. I could not execute the app or diff against upstream, so runtime confirmation and intent are unverified.
candidates.impact: Reflected cross-site scripting in the application origin: an attacker who lures a user to a crafted documentation URL can execute arbitrary JavaScript in that user's browser (subject to cookie flags), e.g. read non-HttpOnly session cookies/tokens, issue authenticated requests, or alter page content. No server-side compromise is required.
candidates.prerequisites: The application installs `new ApiTool().swagger(path)` and/or `.raml(path)`; the UI is enabled by default (`Options.showUI = true`, line 551) and the module does not restrict the UI routes to the dev environment. A victim must open an attacker-supplied link to the documentation path with the crafted `theme` parameter (classic reflected XSS).
candidates.root_cause: ApiTool builds the API-documentation HTML page by string-concatenating the raw `theme` request parameter into the markup. In the Swagger UI handler it is inserted inside a `href="..."` attribute, and in the RAML handler it is inserted into the page body via String.replace; the resulting page is returned with `Results.ok(page).type(MediaType.html)`. No validation, whitelist or HTML/attribute encoding is applied anywhere: `Options.theme(String)` (ApiTool.java 617-620) does not validate, `Mutant.value(String)` returns the raw first parameter value, and the final string is sent through the built-in text renderer, which performs no escaping.
candidates.title: Reflected XSS in ApiTool Swagger/RAML UI via unsanitized `theme` request parameter
candidates.trace: GET /swagger?theme=... -> Router route registered at ApiTool.java 1093 (`router.get(options.path, ...)`) -> `req.param("theme").value(options.theme)` (1094) returns the raw decoded parameter -> `index.replace("<style>", "<link rel=\"stylesheet\" type=\"text/css\" href=\"...theme-" + theme.toLowerCase() + ".css\">...")` (1095-1097) breaks out of the href attribute and injects markup -> `Results.ok(page).type(MediaType.html)` (1099) commits the raw string as HTML -> `BuiltinRenderer.text` (BuiltinRenderer.java 307-314) calls `ctx.type(MediaType.html).send(object.toString())` with no output encoding, so the injected `<script>` is parsed and executed by the browser. The RAML handler at 1035-1041 uses the same unescaped `theme` value in `index.replace("api-console-light-theme.css", "api-console-" + theme + "-theme.css")`.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed; depends on the app mounting ApiTool with UI enabled and on the victim following the crafted link. Could not verify whether this code is upstream-unchanged or an injected regression, nor which release fixed it.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (Cross-site Scripting)

coverage_summary: Visible scope: 4849 files (core `jooby` module, ~90 modules, docs, bundled JS). I read and traced the core request/response pipeline (RequestImpl, ResponseImpl, HttpHandlerImpl, Route/RoutePattern/RouteChain, AssetHandler, Cookie/Session managers, CsrfHandler, CorsHandler, error renderers, Env), and reviewed request/response adapters (ServletServletRequest, Netty/Jetty handlers/SSL) plus selected modules (apitool, assets, pac4j/pac4j2, crash, whoops, livereload, apitool resources, template modules). I searched for common sink patterns (deserialization, exec, file/path resolution, URL fetch, crypto/random, HTML building). Not every module was inspected line-by-line; bundled JS/webjar assets were not reviewed.
limitations: No code execution, build, tests or scanners were run; findings are static-source leads only, not runtime-confirmed.
No upstream reference/commit history is available, so I could not determine whether the ApiTool theme handling is original upstream code or an injected regression, nor which release fixed it.

Only one candidate may be submitted; the selection between the ApiTool XSS and the other XSS/path-traversal/deserialization leads is a judgement call based on attacker control and precondition strength.
Several modules (datastore integrations, asset processors, native websocket/SSE paths) were only skimmed, and third-party webjar resources are outside the snapshot.
App-specific configuration (whether ApiTool UI is mounted in production, cookie flags, CSP/SameSite) could reduce or alter exploitability.

rejected_leads.lead: Default error page `DefaulErrRenderer` writes `message`/stacktrace into HTML without escaping; attacker-influenced Err messages exist (e.g. `CsrfHandler` line 344 includes the raw submitted token, `Err.BadMediaType` includes the raw Accept header).
rejected_leads.reason: Real sink, but the common attacker-controlled 404 path is escaped via `Request.path(true)`; reaching the unescaped cases needs additional app configuration (e.g. CsrfHandler installed, crafted token/header), so it is a weaker, less certain chain than the ApiTool reflection. Left as unconfirmed.

rejected_leads.lead: `FileSystemAssetHandler.resolve` (modules/jooby-assets/.../FileSystemAssetHandler.java 224-231) resolves `source.resolve(path)` with no normalize/startsWith containment check, unlike `AssetHandler.loader` (jooby/.../AssetHandler.java 567-582).
rejected_leads.reason: Only used in the asset-watcher/dev path (`assets.watch` defaults to dev) for configured asset directories/patterns; exploitability depends on the underlying server not normalizing `..` in the request path. Not verified and much narrower than the ApiTool issue.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe Java deserialization (`ObjectInputStream.readObject`) of session values in `modules/jooby-pac4j/.../AuthSerializer.java` 219-230 and `modules/jooby-pac4j2/.../Pac4jSessionStore.java` 272-281.
rejected_leads.reason: Requires an attacker to control a session attribute consumed under a pac4j-managed key; Jooby session stores are server-side or HMAC-signed (cookie store), and no direct attacker-to-session-attribute path was found in this snapshot. Preconditions too uncertain to select.

rejected_leads.lead: CORS default reflects the request `Origin` and sets `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` with `origin: "*"` (CorsHandler.java 284-305, Cors.java 324-332).
rejected_leads.reason: Dangerous documented default/configuration rather than a code-level bypass of a security check; also mitigated by modern browsers' SameSite cookie defaults. Not selected.

rejected_leads.lead: `jooby-crash` exposes an unauthenticated web/HTTP shell (`HttpShellPlugin.install` 225-242, `WebShellPlugin.install` 222-267) allowing command execution.
rejected_leads.reason: This is the explicit purpose of the CRaSH developer tool; it is opt-in and documented as a remote shell, so it is a deployment risk rather than a hidden code vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Server session manager issues unsigned session-ID cookies when `application.secret` is absent (`ServerSessionManager.unsign` 341-350) and does not auto-rotate IDs.
rejected_leads.reason: Design choice with SecureRandom session IDs; fixation/renewal is left to application code (`Session.renewId()`), no exploitable flaw demonstrated in source.

summary: Jooby 1.6.4-SNAPSHOT (4849 visible files: core `jooby` module plus ~90 modules). I traced request input through routing, rendering, sessions, CSRF/CORS, static assets and several modules. The strongest source-evidenced issue is a reflected XSS in the `jooby-apitool` documentation UI: the documented runtime `theme` query parameter is concatenated unvalidated/unescaped into the HTML page returned with `Content-Type: text/html`, so a crafted link executes script in the application origin. Other suspicious spots (default error page not escaping messages, dev asset handler path resolution, pac4j serialization, CORS defaults) are listed as rejected/less-certain leads because their preconditions or attacker control are weaker or unconfirmed.
